items.title: Insurance Claims Are AI's Messiest Data Problem — Denys Linkov, Wisedocs
items.content_snippet: Insurance claims are full of handwriting, faxes, duplicates and 8GB PDFs. Denys Linkov of Wisedocs explains why that unstructured data is both the biggest barrier and the biggest opportunity for AI in insurance. He covers cleaning the data, analysis within a single document, and cross-claim insights, along with the benchmark Wisedocs built with Artificial Analysis to test how models handle medical records. items.title: Evals for High-Stakes AI Agents — Doneyli De Jesus & Annabell Schäfer, Langfuse
items.content_snippet: A hands-on workshop on evaluating AI applications where mistakes are expensive. Annabell Schäfer and Doneyli De Jesus from Langfuse use a banking assistant to walk through the whole AI engineering loop. They cover tracing with PII masking, building datasets, turning domain-expert comments into failure modes, LLM-as-judge and code evaluators, and CI that blocks a prompt change when scores drop. Chapters: - 00:00 Why evals are hard - 05:01 The AI engineering loop - 12:47 Demo: a banking assistant

items.title: Teach Your Agent to Prove It's Done — Nick Nisi & Zack Proser, WorkOS
items.content_snippet: Your agent says it's done. Is it? Nick Nisi and Zack Proser from WorkOS show how to build verification loops that let coding agents check their own work. They cover clear goals, CLI health checks, browser snapshots, LLM judges and evals, so a failure drives the next fix instead of landing on your desk. items.title: An AI Agent Got Its User Banned From Resy — Keycard, JPMorgan Chase & AAuth
items.content_snippet: An AI agent trying to book a restaurant made 200 calls in 90 minutes and got its own user banned from Resy. It had good intentions. It just had no limits. Keycard's Allie Howe moderates a keynote panel with Keycard CEO Ian Livingstone, JPMorgan Chase Global Chief Security Architect Michael Davis, and OAuth co-creator Dick Hardt on why companies still won't hand agents real autonomy, and what has to change. items.title: Stop Chatting With Spreadsheets — Francesco Galletta & Felippe Felisola Caso, Monzo
items.content_snippet: Fast answers are easy to get. Answers you can trust with your money are harder. Francesco Galletta and Felippe Felisola Caso build a financial-analyst agent harness live, using one real problem: paying for a wedding. They show the five design principles they use for AI you can trust: shared domain, consistency, evidence, accountability and verification.
